supersedes.its_verdict: NO-GO at 39affafb (PR #1144): its candidate, after_queue + within_limit, improved 1 of 7 piles
supersedes.why_a_new_one: PR #1154 (#1142) changed the signal that pilot read. Under a --decaps-from intent the emitter now writes decaps.within_radius_refs, the caps the reference keeps within the 5 mm tether search radius, and a listed cap the graded board strands beyond that radius is a decap_ungraded ERROR; on all seven pilot boards it was a WARN. A pilot on a changed signal is a new measurement, so its rule is fixed again before any of its numbers exist.

purpose: Fixes, BEFORE any pile number on the per-cap signal exists, how ONE stage-3.5 variant is measured on #1105's pile basis and what its verdict licenses. Kept from the first pre-registration unless the signal change forces otherwise: the boards, the input, the intent, the seed, the signal key, the guards and their tolerances, and the go rule.

base.on: local branch speedups, 27 commits ahead of origin/main b861d208, not pushed. 47 commits have touched py_placer/placement/seeder.py since the first pilot's 39affafb, so that pilot's numbers are the evidence for the pick below, not a forecast of this run's

input.stager: tests/stress/stage_unaided.py stage(): every non-mechanical part at the outline's bbox centre, rotation 0; the mechanical refs keep their pose and are written to mechanical.json beside the pile
input.where: <row workdir>/pile/<board>; the arms are written OUTSIDE pile/, because stage() arms the unaided provenance regime over its directory

intent.how: the CLI, so mechanical.json is compiled into fixed_poses as a run sees it
intent.signal_change: the argv is the first pilot's; what it writes is not. Since #1142 the same command also writes decaps.within_radius_refs and decaps.within_radius_mm, and the intent's min_reader is 8

seed.engine: seeder.seed_from_intent with random.Random('0') and QUENCH_BASE's floors (clearance 0.2, board_edge_clearance 0.55, grid_step 0.1), no polish
seed.scope: place_seed's own rule without --force: seed_refs = stacked_suspect_refs when the pile is partially unplaced, else every unlocked part

signal_change: the key is the first pilot's; what it counts is not. intent_errors now carries one decap_ungraded ERROR per cap in decaps.within_radius_refs that an arm leaves beyond decaps.within_radius_mm of the chip it tethers to (floorplan.rule_decap_ungraded). The pilot computes none of this: the CLI writes the list and the grade reads it

unread_guards.why: columns the go rule does not read, at the first pre-registration's tolerances: the pilot reports them, and on_go (i) requires none to rise past its tolerance

eligibility.rule: decided from INPUTS before any seed: a board is a trial board iff its emitted pile intent arms decaps.max_distance_mm, writes a non-empty decaps.within_radius_refs, and its seeder_forecast scope is >= 1; a _pile_inputs() refusal (PileIneligible) makes it ineligible
eligibility.changed_from_v1: the held-list clause is new, and forced by the signal change: a board whose intent holds no cap is graded on the first pilot's signal, so it cannot test what this pilot is re-run to test
eligibility.ineligible: seeded and reported like a trial board, never counted toward N; nothing is dropped after seeing an outcome
eligibility.record: per board: whether decaps.max_pin_distance_mm is armed or withheld, and the held list's length

candidate.name: within-limit
candidate.why_one: a best-of-N pick inflates 'improve' under the null (three coin-flip variants give a board at least one 'improve' 7 times in 8), so ONE variant is named here and the other two are diagnostics that cannot change the verdict
why_this_one: Picked from the published #1144 table (measured at 39affafb, before #1154) and #1154's per-pile counts; nothing was measured for the pick.

The signal change charges a held cap left beyond 5 mm. In #1144's table within-limit left fewer caps beyond 5 mm than OFF on every pile that had any: splitflap 8 -> 6, tigard 7 -> 4, watchy 5 -> 2, glasgow 19 -> 6, ulx3s 46 -> 29, orangecrab 17 -> 8 (esp_prog 0 -> 0). The first pilot's candidate, after-queue, left MORE than OFF on 6 of 7 (splitflap 8 -> 10, tigard 7 -> 15, watchy 5 -> 12, glasgow 19 -> 22, ulx3s 46 -> 47, orangecrab 17 -> 18): it is the variant the new signal charges, so re-running it would re-test the pick the evidence already counts against.

The signal change does not touch the guards. On the arbiter guards within-limit raised one on 3 piles (splitflap hpwl 2894.8 -> 2979.1; tigard crossings 434 -> 456; orangecrab crossings 4287 -> 4544 and hpwl 2849.3 -> 2941.2), after-ics on 4 (splitflap hpwl -> 2981.9; tigard crossings -> 440; ulx3s hpwl 7975.2 -> 7997.2; orangecrab crossings -> 4826 and hpwl -> 3067.9), after-queue on 5 (splitflap, tigard, watchy, ulx3s and orangecrab).

after-ics also pulled caps in (6, 3, 3, 7, 36 and 7 left beyond), but it keeps a claimed seat that lands past the decap limit, and its decap errors rose on 4 piles (tigard 2 -> 4, watchy 2 -> 3, ulx3s 0 -> 1, orangecrab 10 -> 21) where within-limit's rose on 3 (tigard 2 -> 3, watchy 2 -> 3, orangecrab 10 -> 12).
candidate.expectation: NOT part of the rule. If the engine still behaved as at 39affafb, within-limit would raise an arbiter guard on splitflap, tigard and orangecrab whatever the signal reads, and esp_prog strands no held cap on a plain seed (#1154: 0) and read neutral; at most 3 of 7 could then improve, short of the 6 the rule needs. The published evidence therefore predicts NO-GO. The pilot is run because the engine has moved since, and the rule is not loosened to meet the prediction.

pilot.how: one invocation over all seven boards, in one process and a fresh workdir outside kicad_files/, at the commit that adds this file. A later commit may change only the measurement's plumbing (no file under py_placer/, py_tools/, py_router/ or rust_router/) and the report names it. A runtime estimate on esp_prog alone (--board esp_prog.kicad_pcb, a partial run that prints no verdict) may be taken first; it is not the pilot
per_arm_report: intent_errors, and its decap_* rules by name
caps beyond the 5 mm radius, count and summed mm (groups.decap_populations' beyond)
the unread guards past their tolerance
pilot.go_rule: the CANDIDATE (within-limit) improves -- signal falls, no arbiter guard rises, intent_errors do not rise -- on >= max(1, N-1) of the N eligible boards, with N >= 3; otherwise NO-GO
pilot.note: the other two variants are diagnostics only and cannot change the verdict; the unread guards and the beyond-radius column are reported, not read, by the go rule

on_go.change: DECAP_LATE_WITHIN_LIMIT on, and stage 3.5 on by default only where this pilot measured it: a seed of a board place_seed reads as a pile (assess_placement unplaced or partially unplaced) in which stage 2.5 has no owner IC seated before it. Whole-board re-seeds of placed boards keep the default off; the corpus decap-within-limit-* rows measured them and stay rejected
on_go.no_ladder: the first pre-registration's ladder (seed both, keep the better) is not carried over: the pilot measures the candidate itself, and a ladder would ship an engine no pilot measured
pass_requires_all: (i) decap-pile-within-limit-<board> rows (input 'pile', the eligible boards) in tests/test_placement_ab.py pass gate() -- >= 3 distinct boards, improve on >= N-1, regress on none -- and no unread guard rises past its tolerance on any of them

(ii) the full placement A/B table with the scoped default: every pinned row keeps its measured mark, every DRIFT is read, and the baseline is re-recorded with --write-baseline in the same commit as the change
(iii) tests/test_placement_probe.py on >= 3 eligible piles, OFF vs ON: routed failed, open and unconnected counts rise on none
on_go.then: the change ships with a regression test, docs, skill text and CLI/GUI parity, per CLAUDE.md

stop_rule: a NO-GO, or any failed on_go condition: STOP, reset fix-1105 to 9af8d492 so the repo carries nothing of this experiment (CLAUDE.md 'Commit only what worked'), and report the full per-pile table to the maintainer; #1105 stays open
